subject: SRW
body: A city report states that the number of cyclists using a new protected lane rose from 420 in April to 610 in June. The report also notes that car traffic on the adjacent street remained nearly unchanged. Which conclusion is best supported?
options: Most new cyclists previously drove cars
The lane was associated with an increase in cycling
The lane reduced traffic across the entire city
The lane caused a decrease in car traffic
explanation: The figures show more cyclists used the lane, but they do not establish why they changed or what happened citywide.

subject: SRW
body: A researcher compared two groups of seedlings. One group received eight hours of light daily; the other received twelve. After three weeks, the second group was taller on average. Which statement most accurately describes the result?
options: The first group received too little light to survive
All plants grow taller when exposed to more than eight hours of light
In this experiment, seedlings receiving twelve hours of light grew taller on average
Light duration is the only factor that affects seedling height
explanation: The result applies to the seedlings and conditions in this experiment; it does not prove a universal rule.

subject: SRW
body: The passage says that a historian used shipping records to estimate how much grain entered a port. The records omit small private vessels. Which limitation follows most directly?
options: The historian cannot compare imports across years
The estimate must include more grain than was imported
The records reveal the exact destination of every shipment
The estimate may undercount the total grain imported
explanation: Because some vessels are missing from the records, the total may be lower than the true amount.

subject: SRW
body: A survey of 800 residents found that 64% supported extending library hours. The survey was sent only to people with active library cards. Which concern is most relevant?
options: The percentage cannot be calculated from survey responses
The sample may not represent residents who do not use the library
The sample is too large to produce useful results
Library-card holders were necessarily opposed to the proposal
explanation: Restricting the survey to library-card holders may exclude residents whose views differ.

subject: SRW
body: A scientist observes that a metal rod expands when heated and contracts when cooled. Which additional observation would best strengthen the claim that the change is reversible?
options: A second rod has a different mass
The rod becomes brighter while heating
The rod returns to its original length after cooling
The rod is stored in a dry room
explanation: Returning to the original length after cooling directly supports reversibility.

subject: SRW
body: In the passage, the word “tentative” most nearly means “The committee offered a tentative schedule, explaining that dates might change after the venue inspection.”
options: provisional
careless
final
detailed
explanation: The possibility of later changes shows that the schedule is provisional.

subject: SRW
body: Why does the author mention the failed prototype in a passage about the development of a low-cost water filter?
options: To show how an early design problem informed later improvements
To argue that the project should be abandoned
To suggest that the filter was more expensive than expected
To introduce an unrelated research question
explanation: The failed prototype provides context for the design changes that followed.

subject: SRW
body: Which choice best describes the function of the final sentence? “The trial involved only one school. Further studies across different regions will be needed before the approach can be widely recommended.”
options: It introduces evidence that contradicts the trial
It restates the research question
It qualifies the scope of the preceding findings
It gives a detailed description of the school
explanation: The sentence limits how broadly the results should be applied.

subject: SRW
body: In context, the phrase “a narrow window” refers to “Because the migratory birds stop at the wetland for only a few days, researchers have a narrow window in which to collect samples.”
options: a small opening in a building
a limited number of research tools
a restricted geographical area
a short period of opportunity
explanation: The birds' brief stay creates a short period for collecting samples.

subject: SRW
body: Which statement best captures the main purpose of the passage? “Several towns have restored neglected canals. The projects have reduced local flooding in some areas and created walking routes. Their success, however, depends on regular maintenance.”
options: To describe the history of water transport
To explain benefits of canal restoration while noting a condition for success
To compare the cost of canals in different towns
To argue that canals should replace roads
explanation: The passage presents benefits and then emphasizes the need for maintenance.

subject: SRW
body: A student wants to emphasize that a new archive is useful to researchers because it makes rare letters searchable online. Which sentence best achieves this goal?
options: By digitizing rare letters and making them searchable, the archive gives researchers easier access to primary sources
The archive contains letters, some of which are rare
Researchers have used archives for many years
The letters were written before the archive was created
explanation: This choice directly connects the searchable digital collection to its research value.

subject: SRW
body: Notes: • Composer A wrote the score in 1912. • The first performance took place in 1915. • The work later became widely performed. Which choice best combines the notes to emphasize chronology?
options: Composer A wrote the score in 1912, and it premiered three years later, in 1915, before becoming widely performed
Composer A wrote many scores, including one that was performed
The work became widely performed, and Composer A wrote it in 1912
The first performance was in 1915, although the composer is unknown
explanation: The sentence preserves the dates and places the events in chronological order.

subject: SRW
body: A student is revising a paragraph about urban trees. Which transition best signals a contrast? “Trees can lower street temperatures during heat waves. _____, young trees require years of care before providing substantial shade.”
options: However
For example
Similarly
Therefore
explanation: “However” introduces a contrast between an immediate benefit and a delayed one.

subject: SRW
body: Notes: • A telescope opened in 2020. • It is located on a high-altitude plateau. • The location reduces atmospheric interference. Which choice most effectively explains why the location matters?
options: High-altitude plateaus are found in several countries
The telescope is used to observe distant objects
Opened in 2020, the telescope sits on a high-altitude plateau, where thinner air reduces atmospheric interference
The telescope opened in 2020 on a plateau
explanation: This choice connects the location directly to its scientific advantage.

subject: SRW
body: Which choice most logically completes the text? “The first survey recorded residents’ preferred transport options. A second survey, conducted six months later, asked the same questions. _____”
options: Residents were not asked about transport
The second survey used a different set of questions
Researchers could therefore compare whether preferences had changed over time
The first survey was distributed after the second
explanation: Repeating the same questions allows comparison over time.

subject: SRW
body: Neither the director nor the actors _____ available for the afternoon rehearsal.
options: is
are
was
has been
explanation: With “neither…nor,” the verb agrees with the nearer subject, “actors,” which is plural.

subject: SRW
body: The collection of maps, including several rare coastal charts, _____ stored in the climate-controlled room.
options: were
have been
are
is
explanation: The subject is the singular noun “collection,” not the plural “maps.”

subject: SRW
body: Which choice completes the sentence according to standard English conventions? “After reviewing the evidence, _____.”
options: the recommendation was revised by the committee
the committee revised its recommendation
the evidence led to a revision
a revised recommendation was issued
explanation: The introductory modifier must describe the subject that follows; the committee reviewed the evidence.

subject: SRW
body: The researcher labelled each sample carefully, _____ the labels were checked by a second technician.
options: but
and
or
for
explanation: “And” correctly joins two related independent clauses.

subject: SRW
body: Which choice uses the apostrophe correctly?
options: The student’s projects were displayed in the hall
The students projects’ were displayed in the hall
The students’s projects were displayed in the hall
The students’ projects were displayed in the hall
explanation: The plural noun “students” takes an apostrophe after the s to show shared possession.

subject: SRW
body: The novel, along with two short stories, _____ included in the course syllabus.
options: have been
are
were
is
explanation: The singular subject “novel” determines the verb; the intervening phrase does not change agreement.

subject: SRW
body: Which choice completes the sentence? “The museum acquired the painting in 1984; _____, it was not displayed until the gallery reopened in 1991.”
options: similarly
for example
therefore
however
explanation: The second clause contrasts with the acquisition date, so “however” is appropriate.

subject: SRW
body: The committee considered three proposals, _____ each addressed a different aspect of the problem.
options: each of which
each
each of them
which each
explanation: “Each of which” correctly introduces a relative clause modifying “proposals.”

subject: SRW
body: A study found that a particular bee species visited 18 plant species in a forest fragment and 11 in a nearby field. Researchers caution that they observed the bees for twice as long in the forest. What is the main limitation?
options: The forest fragment is necessarily healthier
The field must contain fewer plant species overall
The longer observation period may explain some of the difference
The bees cannot visit more than 11 plant species
explanation: Unequal observation time makes the raw counts difficult to compare.

subject: SRW
body: In context, “sustain” most nearly means “The evidence is not sufficient to sustain the claim that the new policy caused the increase.”
options: support
delay
repeat
weaken
explanation: Evidence that sustains a claim supports it.

subject: SRW
body: A student wants to introduce an example that illustrates a general claim about public parks. Which transition is most appropriate?
options: As a result
For instance
Nevertheless
In contrast
explanation: “For instance” introduces a specific example.

subject: SRW
body: By the time the guests arrived, the musicians _____ their instruments.
options: has tuned
tunes
had tuned
will tune
explanation: The past perfect describes an action completed before another past event.
